transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:32 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Sophie Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Liu (Redwood SE), Jenna Ruiz (CTO), Liam O'Connor (Head of ML), Priya Menon (SRE)

[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm Sophie, AE on the Redwood team, and Marco is our SE.
[00:08] Marco: hi all, Marco here. we'll mostly ask questions about your latency targets, concurrency, and then sketch a POC plan.
[00:18] Jenna: thanks. I'm Jenna. quick context — we're a 3PL, real-time shipment ETA predictions, and a new chat assist for operations. latency is... like huge for us. p95 has to be < 300ms for the inline suggestions.
[00:34] Liam: and on the batch side we have high throughput for nightly scoring, but the real pain is concurrent interactive sessions from drivers and operations. around 800-1,200 concurrent users at peak.
[00:50] Priya: also security — we need VPC, KMS integration, and audit logs. SOC2 is a requirement for us.
[00:57] Sophie: got it. when you say p95 < 300ms, is that for the whole end-to-end or inference-only?
[01:06] Jenna: inference-only ideally, network + client adds some overhead. but for evaluation please show both.
[01:12] Marco: that makes sense. couple clarifying Qs: typical prompt lengths, streaming needs, and do you require streaming tokens back as we generate?
[01:22] Liam: prompts are usually 256-1024 tokens depending on context. For chat we do streaming to show partial results — so streaming latency matters a lot.
[01:31] Sophie: okay. and concurrency — you mentioned 800-1,200 concurrent users. how many simultaneous inferences per user?
[01:37] Liam: average 1.2 requests per user per minute during peak, bursty. so sustained concurrency maybe ~1,000 requests/sec at peaks? it's a bit fuzzy.
[01:46] Marco: good to know. for benchmarking we'd recommend a matrix: sequence length buckets 256/512/1024, token generation sizes 32/128, and concurrency buckets 100/500/1000. that lets us estimate tokens/sec and tail latencies.
[02:05] Jenna: what kind of p95 numbers do you see on hosted vs dedicated?
[02:10] Marco: rough numbers — serving a 7B open model on dedicated optimized runtime, p95 for a 256->32 generation can be 120-200ms depending on hardware and quantization. Hosted varies by instance but we can guarantee lower latency on Dedicated with reserved capacity.
[02:24] Sophie: important to call out tradeoffs — cheaper quantized paths reduce tokens/sec but sometimes increase tail variance. Also batching helps cost but can hurt p95.
[02:36] Liam: how about streaming specifically — does the runtime start sending partial tokens earlier?
[02:40] Marco: yes, we support token-by-token streaming. streaming p95 is often dominated by first-token time + per-token micro-latency. For low-latency streaming we tune KV cache warmups and reduce batching windows to minimize first-byte times.
[02:54] Priya: any rough numbers for tokens/sec for the configs? we need to dimension gpus and estimate costs.
[03:00] Marco: example: on a A100-class dedicated pod, serving a quantized 7B, you might see 800-1,500 tokens/sec sustained depending on sequence lengths and batching policies. On less capable GPUs or hosted multi-tenant nodes it could be lower.
[03:14] Jenna: our engineering team is nervous about p95 spikes during cold starts. how do you handle KV cache warmup and cold-starts?
[03:21] Marco: automatic prefix and KV caching helps — we can pin warm caches for dedicated pools. we also recommend gradual traffic ramp up and can keep warm workers for critical routes. fallback policies help if capacity is constrained.
[03:34] Liam: are you able to do per-route p95 SLOs? like 200ms for inference route A and 500ms for background scoring?
[03:41] Sophie: yes that's a common pattern — per-route SLOs and routing policies. can set canary, A/B, and fallbacks to larger models or lower cost variants.
[03:48] Jenna: network-wise — we need VPC with no egress to public internet for PII routes. Private deployment or VPC peering?
[03:56] Marco: we support both. Redwood Private gives on-prem-like control; Dedicated supports customer VPC peering and private networking. can integrate with KMS/HSM for key management.
[04:06] Priya: how about audit logs and retention?
[04:09] Sophie: we can provide per-request audit logs, configurable retention, and masking options. SOC2 cert included in enterprise pack. we'll share the security pack after the call.
[04:18] Liam: great. for the POC we want to run token/sec benchmarks with our 1M token corpus across seq lengths and streaming enabled. can you run that or do we run it?
[04:28] Marco: typically we provide a benchmark harness and can run it in your sandbox or our infra. recommended: we run a baseline on Redwood Hosted, then on Dedicated provisioned to your reserved capacity, and optionally Private if you need VPC/on-prem.
[04:43] Jenna: timeline-wise we want POC kickoff ~Mar 10, and a go/no-go decision by end of March.
[04:50] Sophie: that's reasonable. we'll send template + proposed dates.
[04:53] Liam: quick deep dive — you mentioned batching windows hurting p95. what's your smallest batching window?
[04:58] Marco: we have sub-10ms batching windows in the runtime; operational choices allow you to set maximum latency budget per route, which dynamically controls batching. for strict p95 targets we lean towards smaller windows and more worker parallelism.
[05:11] Priya: any notes on quantization compatibility with streaming? is output quality impacted?
[05:16] Marco: quantization can slightly alter output distribution; for many retrieval-augmented or instruction tasks it's fine, but we encourage evals. streaming works with quantized kernels; we'll include quality regression checks in the POC.
[05:29] Jenna: what about concurrency limits per customer on Hosted?
[05:32] Sophie: Hosted has soft quotas; for guaranteed throughput and SLOs we recommend Dedicated where you get reserved GPU pools and predictable TTFB.
[05:41] Liam: cost exploration — can you give a ballpark cost per 1k requests at our seq sizes?
[05:46] Sophie: we'll include a cost model in the follow-up. rough rule: optimized Dedicated + batching and caching can be 2-3x cheaper per token versus naively self-hosting when you include infra and SRE overhead. exact numbers depend on concurrency and cache hit rates.
[05:59] Marco: also worth modeling the tokens/sec trade-off: aggressive batching increases tokens/sec and lowers cost per token but can raise p95. the POC matrix will help find the sweet spot.
[06:12] Jenna: ok let's walk through what you need from us to start the POC.
[06:16] Marco: we need sample payloads, traffic profile (concurrency, requests/sec), target p95 numbers per route, security constraints (VPC/peering, KMS), and preferred timeline.
[06:26] Liam: we'll export sample prompts and a 1M token corpus, plus traffic metrics.
[06:30] Sophie: perfect. i'll recap the next steps at the end.
[06:35] Jenna: one more technical Q — do you support partial token retries if a worker fails mid-stream?
[06:40] Marco: we have graceful degradation; if a worker fails mid-stream the router can fallback to a different model variant or re-issue the request. partial-token retry is tricky but we can resume by re-sending context and trimming duplicated tokens client-side. we'll document recommended client-side idempotency keys for streaming sessions.
[06:58] Sophie: note — we'll include recommended client-side logic in the POC docs.
[07:03] Liam: great. any limitations on GPU types if we go Dedicated?
[07:07] Marco: we support a range — A100, H100, and cost-optimized options. kernel selection in our runtime will pick best paths; we can benchmark across GPU types to show p95 and tokens/sec differences.
[07:20] Priya: networking — do you support egress control to ensure model updates don't phone home?
[07:25] Marco: yes, Private deployments can be air-gapped and Dedicated VPC peering can limit egress. we'll surface the options in the security pack.
[07:33] Jenna: ok let's discuss the POC success criteria. we want: inference-only p95 < 300ms for route A (chat streaming) at 1,000 concurrent, sustained 1,200 requests/sec, and overall token/sec > 1,000 with 95% cache hit.
[07:49] Marco: audible — we'll map that to a benchmark matrix and show tradeoffs. to be clear, 1k concurrent streaming sessions with p95 < 300ms is ambitious but doable with Dedicated and pinned warm caches; we'll validate in the POC.
[08:01] Sophie: recap coming and confirm next steps.
[08:05] Jenna: quick — any regulatory red flags for us? e.g., EU data residency?
[08:10] Sophie: we support regional hosting and private deployments for data residency. we'll include region options and compliance notes.
[08:17] Marco: also will run an initial bench on Hosted to set a baseline; sometimes Hosted is sufficient if your peak is lower.
[08:25] Liam: ok, go ahead.
[08:28] Sophie: recap — we'll: 1) send benchmark template and sample payloads, 2) share SOC2/security pack + VPC checklist, 3) propose POC kickoff week of 2026-03-10, 4) provision sandbox and run baseline hosted bench, 5) run Dedicated bench after we get traffic profile.
[08:49] Jenna: sounds good.
[08:52] Priya: can you also include a checklist of required network configs so our infra team can pre-approve?
[08:58] Marco: yes we'll include step-by-step peering and firewall rules.
[09:02] Sophie: action items captured. any final q's?
[09:05] Liam: none from me. thanks.
[09:06] Jenna: thanks everyone.
[09:08] Sophie: thanks — we'll follow up by email with the docs and proposed times.

End transcript.

Notes: transcription has minor name/wpm errors typical of automated transcripts. Several times numbers were clarified in follow-up emails (see next steps).
